title: private-deploy-field-scratchpad-2026-03-04
content:
Daily scratchpad: private deploy field notes (customer: Acme Healthcare) - 2026-03-04

OVERVIEW / CONTEXT:
- Onsite/VPC install for Acme Healthcare (PHI). They want on-prem with private control plane + HSM KMS.
- Goal: validate initial install steps, capture blockers & env quirks, hand off to SRE for final runbook.
- Target cluster: 6x A100 nodes (prod-like), containerd, k8s 1.26, NVIDIA drivers + CUDA 12.1.

TODAY'S HIGH-LEVEL TASKS:
- Quick sanity check of preflight checklist for customer infra (network, DNS, NAT, routing).
- Try helm install of redwood-private v0.9.1 in staging cluster replica of customer infra.
- Interview infra lead (Sam) about HSM/KMS integration and firewall exceptions.

QUICK TODO (priority order):
1) Confirm firewall rules with Acme network (ports: 6443, 2379-2380, 10250, 10255, 80/443 egress to S3 endpoint) - ACTION: Sam to confirm; I emailed 03/03.
2) Verify GPU driver compatibility matrix (CUDA 12.1 / driver 535.x) on PRE-PROD VM images - I have one node image failing nvidia-smi after kernel update.
3) Run helm upgrade --install in local k8s mirror cluster; capture helm values used (storage, s3 endpoint, kms config).
4) Document MinIO S3 endpoint override for airgapped: minio.local:9000 + CA bundle -> include in chart values.
5) KMS: get HSM vendor contact & cert chain; need to test PKCS#11 flow.

NOTES / COMMANDS I RAN:
- kubeconfig used: /home/riley/.kube/acme-staging-kubeconfig
- helm command: helm upgrade --install redwood-private ./charts/redwood-private -f values-acme-staging.yml --namespace redwood-system --create-namespace
- kubectl: kubectl -n redwood-system get pods -o wide
- observed: redwood-controller stuck CrashLoopBackOff (probe failed) -> logs show "failed to initialize kv cache: s3 bucket unreachable (x509 error)"

ENV DETAILS / OBSERVED BLOCKERS:
- Customer S3 endpoint uses TLS with custom CA; our init container doesn't have CA bundle mounted by default. Need values to mount /etc/ssl/acme-ca.pem to init containers and envoy.
- HSM: vendor requires outbound TCP to vendor license server on port 443; Acme network policy currently denies outbound to internet. Need formal exception or proxy.
- Kernel mismatch on node-03: nvidia-module didn't load (dkms failed) after kernel-security patch. Risk: must pin kernel to validated version or rebuild driver.
- DNS: internal domain acme.internal not resolvable from pods (coreDNS forwarders not set). Might need stubDomain config in CoreDNS for acme.internal -> internal DNS IPs.

OPEN QUESTIONS:
- Do we allow a local MinIO mirror instead of their S3 for final install? Pros: offline OK. Cons: customer wants centralized object storage for backups. Need decision.
- KMS/HSM certs: do we support PKCS#11 directly in controller, or do we require sidecar that communicates with HSM? (Samira to confirm architecture options).
- Fallback model variant: should runtime be configured to fallback to CPU-only if GPU nodes become unhealthy? For now set policy to "failover: model-variant-cpu" in values.

ACTION ITEMS / OWNERSHIP:
- Riley: add CA mount option to helm chart values + test in staging (ETA 03/05).
- Sam (Acme infra): request firewall exception + confirm NAT/gateway IPs (blocking HSM & S3).
- Maya: follow up on kernel driver repro and escalate to release-eng if we need a hotfix or different node image.
- Samira: confirm KMS integration pattern and whether we need a vendor sidecar.

SHORT INSTALL NOTES (for runbook draft):
- Preflight checklist:
  * Confirm k8s version 1.26, nodes x86_64, containerd configured, kernel <= 5.15 (validated build), NVIDIA drivers 535.x, CUDA 12.1.
  * Open firewall: 6443 (api), 2379-2380 (etcd), 10250 (kubelet), 9000 (MinIO), 80/443 egress to S3/KMS vendor if required.
  * DNS: ensure pods can resolve acme.internal via CoreDNS stubDomain.
  * Storage: NFS or Ceph mount for persistent volumes; test read/write.
  * CA bundle: provide PEMs for any internal TLS endpoints and mount to /etc/ssl/acme-ca.pem.
  * HSM: vendor certs + PKCS#11 config file (path: /etc/hsm/pkcs11.conf).

- Helm values highlights to set:
  * image.registry: internal-registry.acme.internal
  * objectStorage.endpoint: https://minio.local:9000
  * objectStorage.caBundle: /etc/ssl/acme-ca.pem
  * kms.provider: hsm
  * kms.pkcs11.library: /usr/lib/softhsm/libsofthsm2.so (example)
  * fallback.modelVariant: model-variant-cpu

RECENT LINKS / REFERENCES:
- Confluence: CONFLUENCE-PRIV-setup-guide (customer runbook draft)
- Jira: JIRA-PRIV-456 (ticket tracking firewall + HSM work)
- GH: https://github.com/redwood-inference/helm-charts/pull/78 (CA mount patch branch)

RANDOM NOTES / TOSSED IDEAS:
- Could we bake CA bundle into image if customers frequently use private CAs? Pros: simpler; Cons: image churn + security. Prefer values mount for now.
- Consider adding a diagnostic job that runs preflight network checks (S3, KMS, HSM reachability) and outputs a report. Good for handoff.

MEETING LOG (quick):
- 10:30 sync w/ Sam (Acme infra): they will open ticket with network team today for outbound exceptions; asked for exact IPs -> sent 03/04.
- 14:00 call w/ HSM vendor scheduled 03/05 to share PKCS#11 certs + test plan.

NEXT STEPS:
- Patch helm charts with CA mount + push new values branch (riley/ca-mount-2026-03-04).
- Re-run install in staging mirror after Sam confirms firewall rules.
- Draft runbook preflight section and share with Maya + Samira for review.

NOTES-TO-SELF:
- Keep timestamps in runbook steps.
- Save kubeadm/config and node images used for reproducibility.
- Add troubleshooting section: nvidia-driver rebuild steps, how to capture dmesg + dkms logs.

END OF SCRATCHPAD
